keyVerseText: And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
rootMeaning: The name Ἰωσήφ (Iōsḗph) originates from the Hebrew יוֹסֵף (Yôwçêph), meaning "Jehovah has added." This root meaning highlights a divine increase or addition, suggesting that God has graciously provided or multiplied blessings. Beyond the common English transliteration 'Joseph,' the original Hebrew sense enriches our understanding of the name as a testimony to God's providential action in the lives of His people.
usageInScripture: The word Ἰωσήφ appears 35 times in the New Testament, primarily translated as 'Joseph' in 18 instances. Other frequent translations include 'of Joseph' and 'to Joseph,' indicating possessive or relational uses. The name refers to multiple individuals, notably the son of Jacob, the husband of Mary, and other Israelites, underscoring its importance as a common yet theologically significant personal name in Scripture.
theologicalSignificance: The name Joseph carries profound theological weight as it connects to God's faithfulness and provision. Knowing that Joseph means 'Jehovah has added' reminds believers that God actively adds to His covenant people and fulfills His promises. The multiple bearers of this name in Scripture, including the earthly father of Jesus, point to God's sovereign orchestration in salvation history. This name thus anchors the narrative of God's redemptive work, culminating in Christ, whose lineage includes Joseph, affirming God's ongoing blessing and addition to His people.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 1:16 states, 'And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.' Here, the name Joseph identifies the legal earthly father of Jesus, emphasizing his role in the Messiah's genealogy. The meaning of Joseph as 'Jehovah has added' enriches this verse by highlighting God's providential addition of Jesus into the human family line, fulfilling divine promises and underscoring the incarnation's reality through Joseph's protective and obedient role.
